findings.finding: The twelve Tier 2B predicates of phase_01_gate all pass right now, before Phase 1 has run for this topic, on Tier 2B extracted/ content belonging to a different call.
findings.evidence: docs/tier2b_topic_and_call_sources/extracted/ holds seven files written by an earlier MSCA-PF run. Their only topic code is HORIZON-MSCA-2026-PF-01-01. g02_p01 to g02_p06 are non_empty_json and g02_p07 to g02_p12 are source_refs_present; all twelve were evaluated against the current tree and all twelve returned passed. No predicate compares the extracted content to selected_call.json's topic_code.
findings.consequence: Phase 1 could write nothing for HORIZON-CL6-2027-01-BIODIV-01 and phase_01_gate would still release n01, letting Phase 2 consume MSCA expected outcomes as if they were this topic's. That is a fail-open gate, and CLAUDE.md §15 requires the system to prefer explicit gate failure over fabricated completion.
findings.not_fixed_here: The branch constraint holds the gate library, gate evaluator and DAG scheduler unmodified, and this ticket is an intake. The fix belongs to the runner ticket or to Milestone 2: either a topic-consistency predicate over Tier 2B extracted/, or an explicit clearing of extracted/ before Phase 1 runs for a new topic.
findings.recommended_owner: Runner Phases 1 to 6 on the demo; carried into the demo report as a candidate Milestone 2 ticket.

findings.finding: cluster_CL6.grouped.json leaves six of the topic's condition fields empty, including legal_and_financial_setup, which is the field the Phase 7 route turns on.
findings.evidence: The grouped entry's legal_and_financial_setup, admissibility_conditions, eligibility_conditions, technology_readiness_level, procedure and exceptional_page_limits are all empty strings. Counted directly on the file.
findings.consequence: The grouped JSON alone cannot establish the grant type. A skill that reads only the slice sees a topic with no legal or financial set-up and no eligibility conditions, so it would miss both the lump-sum regime and the mandatory Copernicus or Galileo/EGNOS condition. The call extract carries both with their own spans, so the slice is not the sole path to them.
findings.not_fixed_here: The grouped JSON is a source aggregation. Repairing it would modify a Tier 2B source to suit this project, which §13.11 forbids. It is registered in the document registry as a derived aggregation rather than a prevailing source.
findings.correction: An earlier draft of this report also claimed the grouped JSON carried U+FFFD replacement characters where the PDF carried typographic quotation marks. That claim was false. The file contains zero U+FFFD; the replacement characters were an artefact of the console encoding used to inspect it, not of the data. Recorded here rather than deleted, because the registry entry for the grouped JSON repeated the same false claim and a reader of either artifact's history deserves to know it was withdrawn.

findings.finding: The work programme directory names do not match their cluster numbers. cluster_CL6.grouped.json and the Part 9 PDF both live under work_programmes/cluster_climate/, although Part 9 is Cluster 6, Food, Bioeconomy, Natural Resources, Agriculture and Environment.
findings.evidence: GROUPED_JSON_MAP in runner/call_slicer.py maps cluster_climate to cluster_CL6.grouped.json and cluster_food to cluster_CL5.grouped.json.
findings.consequence: selected_call.json must record work_programme as 'cluster_climate' for the Call Slicer to resolve, which reads as wrong to a human and is right to the engine. The Part 9 PDF is stored beside its grouped JSON so a topic's sources stay together.
findings.not_fixed_here: Renaming the directories changes GROUPED_JSON_MAP and every call binding that names a work programme area. That is an engine change, outside an intake ticket.

findings.finding: The ticket's first acceptance criterion reads 'call_extracts/HORIZON-CL6-2027-01-BIODIV-01.json and .slice.json exist and cite the Part 9 PDF by page'. The slice cites no PDF and no page. It names only cluster_CL6.grouped.json.
findings.evidence: The slice is written by runner/call_slicer.py, whose output shape is fixed: topic_code, source_grouped_json, source_destination, call_entry, sliced_by, slice_timestamp. It has no field for a page reference and no access to the PDF.
findings.consequence: The criterion is met by the pair, not by each file. The call extract cites the PDF by page; the slice cites the grouped JSON it was sliced from, which is its own honest provenance. Hand-adding a PDF page to the slice would break the byte-equal replay check that proves it was not hand-written, so it was not done.
findings.not_fixed_here: Changing the slicer's output shape is an engine change and would alter the existing CL4 and MSCA slices. The criterion is ticked on the reading above, and that reading is recorded here so the tick is not taken for more than it is.
findings.status: Confirmed, criterion met by the pair

verification: tests/test_tier2b_biodiv_intake.py, 46 checks, all passing. Every source span in the call extract is re-read from the stored PDF and matched against the page it names; mutating one character of one quote turns the check red, which was tried. The three expected outcomes, the five scope requirements and the scope summary are plain strings rather than span objects, so each is separately matched against the topic's pages: a length check alone would have passed on fabricated text. The slice is regenerated by runner/call_slicer.py into a throwaway root and compared field by field, timestamp aside, so the check cannot rewrite the tracked artifact. Each registered document's sha256 and byte count are recomputed on the basis its entry declares: raw bytes for the PDF, LF-normalised bytes for the two JSON sources, because core.autocrlf is true here and a raw digest of a text file would identify the platform rather than the content. Every registry row is checked against the schema the registry declares. The reader is a hard import, not an importorskip, so an environment without pymupdf fails rather than reporting green on checks that never ran. The full suite reports 27 failed and 4957 passed; the 27 are the pre-existing baseline, and the twelve files carrying them were re-run with and without selected_call.json present with identical results, which is what establishes that none is caused by this change.
